subject: astronomy

moments.title: Kennedy commits to the Moon
moments.who: President John F. Kennedy, US Congress
moments.body: On 25 May 1961, Kennedy commits the US to landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely 'before this decade is out'. The Soviets had just launched Gagarin (12 April 1961). Apollo budget peaks at 4.4% of US federal spending in 1966.
moments.takeaway: A political commitment in May 1961 produced a Moon landing in July 1969 — eight years from commitment to footprint.

moments.title: Apollo 11 lands
moments.who: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins
moments.body: On 20 July 1969 at 20:17 UTC, Armstrong and Aldrin land on Mare Tranquillitatis. Armstrong steps onto the surface at 02:56 UTC on 21 July. 600 million people — a fifth of humanity — watch live. Margaret Hamilton's onboard guidance software handles a 1202 alarm during landing without crashing.

quote.text: That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind.

moments.takeaway: The Apollo Guidance Computer ran on 4KB of RAM and 72KB of ROM. Modern AAA batteries are programmed with more code than landed humans on the Moon.

now.title: Lunar exploration today
now.body: After Apollo 17 (1972), no humans returned to the Moon for 50+ years. China's Chang'e program has landed rovers (2013-) and returned samples (2020, 2024 including first far-side return). NASA's Artemis program targets human return in the late 2020s. SpaceX, Blue Origin and private actors are now major spaceflight players.
now.open_questions: Will humans build permanent lunar habitats this century? Water ice at the lunar south pole is the strategic resource.

reflection: Of the 12 men who walked on the Moon (all American men), 4 remain alive in 2026. The longest-living Apollo astronaut, Buzz Aldrin, turned 96 this year. Living memory of human presence on another world is ending.
